memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Pharaoh's daughter went down to the Nile to bathe, and her attendants were walking along the riverbank. She saw the basket among the reeds and sent her female slave to get it. She opened it and saw the baby. He was crying, and she felt sorry for him. "This is one of the Hebrew babies," she said." - Exodus 2:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Of all the people who could have found that basket, it was Pharaoh's own daughter — the daughter of the man who ordered the killing. She opens it, sees a crying baby, and something in her breaks. She knows immediately that he is a Hebrew, and she has compassion anyway.

God is astonishing in how He arranges rescue. He does not always send help from the people we expect. Sometimes He moves the heart of someone outside our circle, outside our community, even outside our faith, to show us kindness.

There is also a challenge here. She could have looked away. Recognising him as a Hebrew gave her every social reason to close the basket and walk on. Compassion cost her something.

Jesus told a story about exactly this — a Samaritan who crossed a divide when religious men walked past (Lk 10:33). The question is not who deserves my compassion. The question is whether I will stop.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have I received unexpected kindness that was really God's provision?
2. Whose need have I noticed recently and walked past?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the kindness You have sent me through unexpected people. Give me a heart that stops when I see someone in need. Amen.
